assertion: The number of longer-term New Yorkers (excluding new arrivals) sleeping each night in NYC DHS shelters increased by 27 percent — or by 12,442 people — during the four years of the Adams administration (January 2022 through December 2025).
article_value: +27% / +12,442 people (as stated once, in the webpage's introduction), Jan 2022–Dec 2025
table: No table in this corpus carries this data (same list_tables(schema='housing') enumeration as above; no nightly/monthly shelter-census time series exists anywhere in this corpus, and no SQL was run since no relevant table exists).
independent_value: 27% / 12,443 people — the report PDF's own Executive Summary, Section II body text, and Figure 2.2 caption all consistently state 12,443, not 12,442; the 12,442 figure appears only once, in the webpage's introductory paragraph, and is very likely a transcription inconsistency within the Coalition's own materials rather than a data disagreement. Independently corroborated in DIRECTION (not magnitude, and not the same measure) by HUD's 2024 Annual Homeless Assessment Report (AHAR) Part 1, fetched directly: 'Between 2023 and 2024, New York saw a 53 percent increase [in PIT sheltered homelessness]... New York City... accounted for almost 88 percent of the increase in sheltered homelessness in New York City' — a single-night January PIT count, a different methodology and window than the Coalition's DHS annual/nightly-census figure, so it corroborates the general trend (rapid NYC shelter growth) but cannot verify the specific 27%/12,443 figure.
